# Spec — Deterministic component update scheduling
<!-- Generated by /skill:sdd-spec on 2026-08-07. Source: finalized grill define-a-stable-component-update-order-contract--20260806-ffc50aea, originating from issue #23. Status: implemented -->
<!-- SDD-Tracking: issue=chichex/waica#23; grill=define-a-stable-component-update-order-contract--20260806-ffc50aea -->

## Context

`Game.tick` currently dispatches `Component.onUpdate` in `entity.components` insertion order (`packages/engine/src/game.ts:208-212`), while prefab resolution preserves JSON order and appends inline components (`packages/engine/src/scene.ts:103-123`). The editor groups cards without exposing that runtime sequence, and `Health` already contains a two-frame workaround for either ordering relative to `StateMachine`. This spec replaces authored order with the component-owned, deterministic schedule confirmed by the finalized grill for issue #23.

## Expected behavior

- **CA-1 (ALTA) — Public scheduling contract.** `ComponentClass` exposes inherited static metadata `updateAfter?: readonly string[]`. The `@waica/engine` root publicly exports a pure `resolveComponentUpdateSchedule` API and typed result/issue contracts. Given an effective entity component-name list plus the complete class metadata/registry, a valid result contains every updateable component exactly once in executable order and no issues; passive components are omitted. An invalid result contains typed, actionable issues and no executable order.

- **CA-2 (ALTA) — Canonical valid ordering.** For every source-array permutation of the same effective component set, the resolver returns the same order. Directed `updateAfter` edges win over the tie-break; simultaneously ready nodes sort ascending by case-sensitive Unicode code-unit `componentName`, never locale. A target known to the registry but absent from the entity creates no edge and no issue. Repeated names inside one `updateAfter` list collapse to one edge. Static metadata follows normal inheritance: a subclass inherits when it declares nothing and replaces, rather than concatenates, when it declares its own list.

- **CA-3 (ALTA) — Invalid schedule semantics.** Only a class whose prototype chain implements `onUpdate` may declare `updateAfter` or be its target. The resolver rejects and identifies: an unknown target (neither a present sibling nor a registered class), a passive declarer or target, a self-edge, any multi-node cycle, and duplicate sibling `componentName` values. Each issue names the relevant components and cause. A present programmatically added sibling establishes its identity even when `Game.registry` is absent.

- **CA-4 (ALTA) — Runtime dispatch and isolation.** Each entity snapshots one resolved schedule when its turn begins. `Game.tick` dispatches only that schedule: a component added during the entity's turn first updates on its next turn, while one added before a later entity's turn is eligible that frame. An invalid entity dispatches no `onUpdate`; valid entities before and after it still update. Runtime emits one diagnostic per unchanged invalid composition, including entity name and causes, and emits again only after composition changes. It never throws from the loop, runs a partial schedule, or falls back to source order.

- **CA-5 (ALTA) — Lifecycle boundary remains intact.** Entity iteration order, `Game.onUpdate`, input end-of-frame handling, collision timing, and the existing dispatch semantics of `onReady`, `onCollide`, `onContact`, and `onDestroy` remain unchanged. Tests characterize those hooks independently of the new `onUpdate` schedule.

- **CA-6 (ALTA) — Shipped read-after-write relations are explicit.** The shipped classes declare exactly these new relations: `AnimatedSprite → StateMachine`; `Health → StateMachine`; `OutOfBounds → DynamicBody, Health, StateMachine`; and example `Gun → StateMachine`. `DynamicBody`, `Lifetime`, and `StateMachine` declare none. `Health` settles deferred graph death on its first eligible update after `StateMachine`, removing the two-frame authored-order workaround without changing successful death, fallback destruction, revival, or invulnerability behavior. ADR-0003 and its code comments describe the new schedule rather than prefab order. Every stock template/example composition resolves without issues, and permuting its component arrays does not change its effective schedule or the tested read-after-write outcomes.

- **CA-7 (ALTA) — Editor visibility without order authoring.** Entity and prefab inspector cards for updateable components render a read-only `update N` badge and, when non-empty, `after: A, B` detail from the effective schedule. Multi-selection renders the concrete value when all selected entities agree and `update varies` otherwise. Invalid compositions render an actionable inline error naming the entity/components/cause instead of a position. Passive cards show no update badge. Play remains available so runtime fail-closed behavior can be diagnosed. No component scheduling drag control is introduced, and card grouping/source serialization is never presented as execution order.

- **CA-8 (ALTA) — MCP introspection.** Every installed-package component row returned by `list_components` includes `updates: boolean` and `updateAfter: string[]`, including empty arrays. Existing provenance, defaults, params, display names, and the textual `projectOwned` boundary remain unchanged; `list_components` does not begin executing project-owned code.

- **CA-9 (ALTA) — MCP validation.** `validate_project` applies the same resolver semantics to package and executable project-owned metadata and to each relevant prefab/effective inline composition. It emits severity `error` findings with stable codes `duplicate-component`, `invalid-update-constraint`, and `component-update-cycle`, making `ok: false`. Class-contract findings point to the declaring project source when available; composition findings appear once at the prefab or effective inline entity that introduces them and are not repeated for every untouched prefab instance. Known-but-absent targets produce no finding. Existing component-load isolation/finding behavior remains unchanged.

- **CA-10 (ALTA) — Documentation, scaffolds, and published shape.** A publishable `packages/engine/README.md` documents lifecycle order, `updateAfter`, conditional co-presence, canonical tie-breaking, invalid schedules, and a concrete example; the root README links it. Generated component scaffolds contain no placeholder `updateAfter`. `docs/adr/0003-health-is-the-damage-model.md` is reconciled with ADR-0004 without changing its damage-model decision. Build and packed-package checks prove the engine root exports the new public API/types and the package includes its README. No new npm dependency is introduced.

- **CA-11 (NULA) — Human game-feel gate.** After every autonomous gate passes and the PR exists, a human plays the platformer example and confirms representative movement, jump/landing, shooting, damage/death, and respawn still feel correct. This gates merge and issue closure, not PR creation.

## Out of scope

- Backward-compatible authored-order mode, prefab/scene schema versions, migrations, or backfills.
- `updateBefore`, phases, numeric priorities, prefab-level overrides, or required-component declarations.
- Scheduling entity order, `Game.onUpdate`, state hooks inside `StateMachine`, or any component hook other than `onUpdate`.
- Component drag-and-drop ordering or generated scaffold metadata.
- Scripted Playwright infrastructure, new npm dependencies, issue #27 subprocess isolation, publishing, or autonomous merge.

## Verifiability

Mixed, without averaging: **CA-1 through CA-10 are ALTA** because the current contract verifies deterministic Vitest unit/integration tests (`pnpm test`), cross-workspace types (`pnpm typecheck`), bundles (`pnpm build`), and packed public/CLI shape (`pnpm test:dist`) locally without services. Inspector output is directly observable through React DOM/static rendering with existing React and happy-dom dependencies; MCP behavior is directly observable through the repository's existing temporary-project fixtures. **CA-11 is NULA** because `.sdd/project.md` explicitly lists game feel as human-only. There are no active PR-size, coverage, dependency, or commit-policy conflicts; lack of PR CI makes the full local ladder mandatory.

## Verification plan

1. **Engine TDD — CA-1..CA-5.** Add focused pure resolver tests plus happy-dom `Game` integration tests. Assertions cover all permutations of a small graph, canonical tie-breaking, inheritance, repeated edges, every invalid cause, programmatic siblings, diagnostic deduplication, fail-closed entity isolation, dynamic additions before/during turns, and characterization of non-`onUpdate` hooks. Run with focused `pnpm exec vitest run <engine test paths>` during red/green cycles, then `pnpm test`.
2. **Shipped behavior TDD — CA-6.** Extend animation/state, Health, OutOfBounds, and example Gun tests to prove each declared edge observes same-frame producer state under reversed source arrays; prove Health fallback/revival/invulnerability outcomes remain unchanged with first-eligible-update settlement; validate every stock prefab composition and its permutations.
3. **Editor component tests — CA-7.** Render the schedule annotation/error UI with existing React DOM/static-rendering and happy-dom facilities in `.test.ts` files included by `vitest.config.ts`. Assert exact badge/detail/error text, passive omission, entity/prefab behavior, multi-selection equality/`varies`, enabled Play, and absence of a scheduling drag affordance.
4. **MCP fixture tests — CA-8..CA-9.** Extend `introspection.test.ts`, project-component-loader fixtures, and focused validation fixtures. Assert exact response fields, codes, severity, `ok`, file/ref attribution, package/project metadata parity, known-absent behavior, effective prefab+inline cycles/duplicates, and no duplicate findings for untouched instances.
5. **Docs/package assertions — CA-10.** Assert the engine README contract and root link, absence of `updateAfter` in generated scaffold output, reconciled ADR wording, root export/type availability, packed README, and no package dependency additions.
6. **Full autonomous ladder — CA-1..CA-10.** From repository root run, in order: `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm test`; `pnpm build`; `pnpm test:dist`. No step may be omitted because PR CI does not exist. Start `pnpm dev`, wait for the printed Vite URL, require `curl -sf <url>` to return 200, then stop the server; report that this proves boot only, not game feel.
7. **Human protocol — CA-11.** After the PR is open: (a) run `pnpm dev` and open the reported URL; (b) verify there are no component-schedule errors in the console; (c) move both directions and jump/land repeatedly; (d) press `F` while facing each direction and verify projectiles use the current facing; (e) damage or kill a slime and exercise player damage/death; (f) fall out of bounds or otherwise trigger respawn; (g) pass only if controls, animation transitions, collision timing, death beat, and respawn feel correct. Record the human result on the PR before merge. The agent never merges.

## Risks and gaps

- `[CONFIRMED]` There is no external user project requiring authored-order compatibility, even though canonical ordering changes the shipped demo's global schedule.
- A missed read-after-write relation can remain deterministic while still being wrong; the shipped-component audit, permutation tests, and human gate are all required.
- Failing closed intentionally freezes one invalid entity, so diagnostics must remain actionable and non-spamming.
- `validate_project` still executes trusted project-owned code in-process; issue #27 may isolate it later but does not block this spec.
- `list_components` deliberately remains textual for project-owned code, so deep project-owned schedule validation belongs to `validate_project`.
- No scripted browser e2e or coverage tooling exists. DOM behavior is covered deterministically; subjective game feel remains CA-11 NULA.
- No CI runs on PRs; all autonomous evidence comes from the required local ladder and must be copied into the PR.
